title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description:
# Binary Tree Right Side View

Given the `root` of a binary tree, imagine standing on the **right side** of the tree. Return the values of the nodes that are visible from top to bottom.

At each depth, only the rightmost existing node is visible. If the right subtree ends before a deeper left-side branch, that deeper left-side node is still visible because it is the only node at its depth.

Example trees use a level-order display: list the root, then each existing node's left and right children in node order. `null` means an absent child; trailing nulls may be omitted. A tree node stores `val`, `left`, and `right`; tree parameters or return values in code are `TreeNode` objects.

## Example 1:

**Input:** root = [1,2,3,null,5,null,4]
**Output:** [1,3,4]
**Explanation:** From the right side, the visible nodes by depth are 1, 3, and 4.

## Example 2:

**Input:** root = [1,null,3]
**Output:** [1,3]

## Example 3:

**Input:** root = []
**Output:** []

## Constraints:

* The number of nodes in the tree is in the range `[0, 100]`.
* `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`

examples.explanation: From the right side, the visible nodes by depth are 1, 3, and 4.

tests.description: Canonical sparse tree where the rightmost visible nodes are not always direct right children.
Empty tree has no visible nodes.
Single-node tree view is the root.
A left child is visible when it is the only node on its level.
A deeper left branch becomes visible after the right side ends.
Sparse children require judging visibility by level, not by following only right pointers.
The rightmost node at one depth can come from a left child of the right subtree.
Negative values do not affect visibility order.
Duplicate values should be returned by level, not deduplicated.
Boundary-valued nodes remain ordinary visible candidates.
Left-side depth can remain visible after a shallow right child ends.

solutions.name: BFS - Last Node per Level
solutions.description:
## Approach

Traverse the tree level by level from left to right. At the beginning of each level, snapshot the queue size, process exactly that many nodes, and append the value of the last node processed for that level.

## Key Insight

The right-side view is one value per depth: the rightmost existing node on that level. Standard left-to-right BFS already visits level nodes in order, so the final node in each level is the visible node.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(w), where w is the maximum number of nodes held in the queue for one level.

solutions.name: DFS - Right First
solutions.description:
## Approach

Run preorder DFS but visit the right child before the left child. Whenever the traversal first reaches a depth that has not been recorded yet, append that node value to the answer.

## Key Insight

Right-first DFS reaches the rightmost visible node at a depth before any node farther left at the same depth. Checking `depth == result.size()` records only that first visible node.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(h), where h is the height of the recursion stack.

solutions.name: Left-First DFS Overwrite
solutions.description:
## Approach

Visit the left child before the right child and keep one answer slot for every depth. The first node creates the slot, and later nodes at the same depth overwrite it.

## Key Insight

With left-first traversal, right-side nodes at a depth are reached later than left-side nodes. Overwriting the stored value therefore leaves the rightmost visible node for that depth.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(h), where h is the height of the recursion stack.

solutions.name: Right-to-Left BFS - First Node per Level
solutions.description:
## Approach

Traverse the tree level by level, but enqueue the right child before the left child. For each level, append the first node removed from the queue and then finish scanning the rest of the level.

## Key Insight

Changing the child enqueue order makes BFS visit each level from right to left. In that order, the first node at a level is exactly the node visible from the right side.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(w), where w is the maximum number of nodes held in the queue for one level.
